The request and the answer are described under that route in the [Controller API](/reference/controller-api/). The body is the config as raw YAML text and is forwarded byte for byte. post.description: Forwards to the controller's `POST /enrollments` (see the [Controller API](/reference/controller-api/)). Where the controller needs a step-up proof, the body may carry the step-up **passphrase** as a string `step_up`: the console fetches the controller's salt (`GET /enrollments/step-up`), derives the key, signs this exact request with a short expiry and forwards the signed assertion instead. The passphrase is never logged or stored. The answer carries the code, so it is sent `Cache-Control: no-store`. A controller with no step-up key answers `409` to a body with a passphrase. At most 4 KiB.

post.description: Removes the operator tags of nodes the aggregator no longer lists. Nothing is deleted unless the body names what to delete, as the operator saw it in the answer to a call without names: the aggregator forgets everything on a restart, so right after one it lists only the few nodes that have pushed so far and \"unlisted\" is not yet \"retired\". Only names that are both confirmed and still unlisted are removed. With `dry_run=true` nothing is removed whatever the body says. It refuses (`409`) when the aggregator lists no node at all.

parameters.description: `true` only reports; `false` (the default) removes the confirmed names. Anything else is `400`.
parameters.name: dry_run

requestBody.description: The names to remove, as listed by an earlier call. May be empty.

200.description: What is unlisted and what was removed.

400.description: `dry_run` is not `true` or `false`, or the body is not `{"names": [...]}`.

409.description: The aggregator lists no nodes, so nothing is pruned.

502.description: A delete failed (the body then also carries `removed`, what went before it), or the controller or aggregator answered something unexpected.

post.description: Checks the credentials and sets the session cookie `wayhouse_ui_session` (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` when the console serves HTTPS itself). With `--users-file` the body needs `username` and `password` and the user's role becomes the session's role; with `--ui-password-file` only `password` is read and the session is an admin; with neither the console is open, any password is accepted and the session is an anonymous admin. Attempts are throttled per client address and per username; a wrong user and a wrong password answer alike. A browser request must be same-origin (`Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Origin`), else `403`.

200.description: Signed in. The `Set-Cookie` header carries the session. Body: `ok` (plain text).

429.description: Too many attempts. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait.

503.description: Too many sessions of a higher role are open already; try again later (plain text).

post.description: Revokes the session named by the cookie, if there is one, and expires the cookie. Signing out without a valid session is not an error.

200.description: Signed out. Body: `ok` (plain text).

get.description: Answers for any valid session, so a page can check on load whether it is signed in and what it may do. With no login configured every request is an anonymous admin.

200.description: The session.

403.description: The session's role is below the one this route needs (`forbidden`, plain text), or the browser marked the request cross-site.

get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket that carries the live fleet view: the first text message is the current view and another follows each update the aggregator reports. Each message is a JSON array of the objects the aggregator's `GET /fleet/subscribe` sends (see the [Aggregator API](/reference/aggregator-api/)). All sockets share one subscription, so the aggregator sees a single subscriber. The socket closes with code 1008 when its session ends (sign-out, idle timeout, maximum age or eviction); the session is re-checked every 30 seconds and before each message. With no aggregator configured the console sends the text `no aggregator configured` and closes. At most 256 sockets are open at once; another upgrade gets `503`. Over HTTP/2 the browser opens the socket as an extended `CONNECT`. A cross-site upgrade is refused with `403`.

403.description: The session's role is below the one this route needs (`forbidden`, plain text), or the browser marked the request cross-site.

503.description: Too many sockets are open (plain text).
